ontology.note: Emits an fw:NetworkReachability activity carrying fw:originCount, fw:reachedNodeCount, fw:travelBudgetMetres, fw:travelBudgetMinutes, fw:assumedSpeedMetresPerMinute, fw:travelMode, fw:travelDirection, fw:edgeLengthSource and, when origins were left out or routed across unmapped ground, fw:unconnectedSiteCount, fw:unconnectedSites, fw:offNetworkSiteCount and fw:offNetworkSites, and prov:used the site source. When it attaches origins to the network itself, it also carries fw:attachedOriginCount, fw:attachmentLimitMetres when a limit is set, and the metric CRS it measured nearest in.

changes.description: On the standard Inspector: one sentence of what it finds, every setting in Configure…, which holds Apply while the speed is outside the mode's range, and the run's counts in the Result. Moved off the old catchment panel to metric-steps-ui.ts. A manual page.

evidence.note: Eleven unit checks cover junctions inside a 200 m budget being returned and a 300 m one not; travelled plus remaining equalling the budget at every junction; the cheapest route deciding the cost, where a 400 m direct street loses to 100 plus 100 through a third junction; inbound and outbound differing on a one-way street in both directions; an origin without a networkNodeId failing with a message naming the snap step; an origin snapped to a different network being refused rather than dropped; per-origin sets tagged by origin; the constant speed and the trusted street lengths both appearing in the notes; a node beyond the budget being discovered but never settled; refusal of an impossible budget, speed, direction or label; a speed outside its mode's plausible band being refused in both directions, where 400 m/min labelled walking is reported as 24 km/h against a 1.8 to 6.6 km/h band; the 1854 Soho 75 m/min sitting inside the walking band, since that is where the band came from; public transport being refused with its reason; and the mode and the km/h travelling in both the notes and the receipt. One check runs the real composition: snapping then reachability over the 738-node Soho network the John Snow example ships, at its own 5 minutes and 75 m per minute, reaching 142 junctions. Not established: that the reached set is what anyone can actually reach. Parity against NetworkX ego_graph with distance='length' is not done. 0.6.0: tests/reachable-inspector.browser.mjs through Configure… and Apply; Chromium, 2026-11-23.
